questions.stem: Epidural analgesia for labour is especially favoured in which obstetric condition?
Epidural anaesthesia can supplement general anaesthesia for which type of surgery?
For which surgery types can an epidural serve as the primary anaesthetic?
questions.answer: Abdominal, thoracic and lower limb surgery.

questions.stem: For ambulatory surgery, which techniques are usually preferred over an epidural?
In children, when is an epidural, especially a caudal, usually placed?
Which epidural technique combines an intrathecal dose with an epidural catheter in one procedure?
How do the physiological effects and contraindications of epidural anaesthesia compare with spinal?
questions.answer: They are much the same as for spinal anaesthesia.

questions.stem: Compared with peripheral nerve blocks for analgesia, what do epidurals usually have?
Which surface landmark marks the C7 spinal level?
Which surface landmark marks the T3 spinal level?
options: Root of the spine of the scapula

questions.stem: Which surface landmark marks the T7 spinal level?
Which surface landmark marks the L1 spinal level?
options: Root of the spine of the scapula

questions.stem: Which surface landmark marks the L4 spinal level?
What is the purpose of giving an epidural test dose?
questions.answer: To exclude intravascular or intrathecal catheter placement.

questions.stem: Before an epidural test dose, what do you look for when aspirating the catheter?
After giving an epidural test dose, when should the patient be assessed?
questions.answer: At once, and every 3-5 min after.

questions.stem: What adrenaline dose is in the classic epidural test dose of lidocaine?
After an epidural test dose, what should be checked on the sensory and motor side?
questions.answer: Onset and level; some onset is expected, but not too fast.

questions.stem: Which systemic symptoms should you ask about after an epidural test dose?
questions.answer: Dizziness, tinnitus, metallic taste and palpitations.

questions.stem: With an adrenaline test dose, which heart rate change suggests intravascular injection?
options: A rise of 10 beats/min within 1 min
A rise of 3 beats/min within 1 min
A rise of 30 beats/min within 1 min
A fall of 10 beats/min within 1 min

questions.stem: How is an epidural loaded with local anaesthetic, in increments?
Why is there a 3-5 min gap between epidural loading increments?
questions.answer: It allows assessment of response and avoids systemic toxicity.

questions.stem: How should epidural top-up doses be handled?
questions.answer: Treat them like loading doses; confirm catheter position first.

questions.stem: What determines how far an epidural local anaesthetic spreads?
How much local anaesthetic per segment is used for a lumbar epidural?
How much local anaesthetic per segment is used for a thoracic epidural?
How much local anaesthetic per segment is used for a caudal epidural?
Why is epidural onset delayed at L5-S1 after lumbar injection?
What volume per segment is commonly used for short patients (5 ft 2 in or less) in place of 2 ml?
Under the Bromage rule, how much is added per segment for each 2 in of height above 5 ft?
Which epidural maintenance option gives more cardiovascular stability?
Compared with continuous infusion, which epidural maintenance option gives better spread?
